question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Vasco da Gama — Ports/Places visited on his first voyage to India (1497–99)]
options: Calicut — First Indian port where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498
Malindi — East African port where da Gama obtained a pilot (Ibn Majid) for the Indian Ocean crossing
Mozambique — Portuguese encountered Arab traders here during the first voyage
Goa — Vasco da Gama established the first Portuguese trading factory here on his first voyage
wrong_fact: Goa was NOT where da Gama established a trading factory on his first voyage. He landed at Calicut (Kozhikode) in 1498. Goa was conquered later by Albuquerque in 1510.
explanation: Vasco da Gama's first voyage (1497–99) took him around the Cape of Good Hope, along the East African coast (Mozambique, Malindi), across the Indian Ocean with the help of the Arab navigator Ahmad ibn Majid, and finally to Calicut (Kozhikode) on 20 May 1498. He did NOT visit or establish a factory at Goa — that city was captured by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510, a decade after da Gama's first voyage.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Vasco da Gama — Voyages and associated events]
options: First Voyage (1497–99) — Discovered the sea route from Europe to India via the Cape of Good Hope
Second Voyage (1502–03) — Led a large fleet to India; bombarded Calicut and secured trade treaties
Third Voyage (1524) — Appointed Viceroy of Portuguese India; died at Cochin (Kochi)
Cape of Good Hope — First rounded by Vasco da Gama in 1497 during his pioneering voyage
wrong_fact: The Cape of Good Hope was NOT first rounded by Vasco da Gama. It was first rounded by Bartolomeu Dias in 1488, nearly a decade before da Gama's voyage.
explanation: Bartolomeu Dias was the first European to round the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, calling it 'Cabo das Tormentas' (Cape of Storms). It was King John II of Portugal who renamed it 'Cape of Good Hope'. Vasco da Gama used this knowledge to successfully navigate the full route to India in 1497. Da Gama's third voyage in 1524 was as Viceroy of Portuguese India; he died at Cochin (present-day Kochi) on 24 December 1524.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Vasco da Gama — Geographic and diplomatic details of his India voyages]
options: Zamorin of Calicut — The Hindu ruler who received Vasco da Gama at Calicut in 1498
Anjediva Island — Da Gama anchored here on the Konkan coast before reaching Calicut on his first voyage
Hormuz — Da Gama's fleet attacked Arab ships near this strait on the second voyage to weaken Muslim trade
Cannanore (Kannur) — Portuguese established their first permanent trading factory (feitoria) in India here after da Gama's second voyage
wrong_fact: Da Gama's second voyage (1502–03) attacked Arab and Calicut ships near the Indian coast and Malabar region — he did NOT specifically attack ships near the Strait of Hormuz. The Hormuz conquest is associated with Afonso de Albuquerque (1515).
explanation: On his second voyage (1502–03), Vasco da Gama led a fleet of 20 ships and brutally attacked Muslim merchant vessels off the Malabar Coast (notably burning the Miri ship with 200–400 pilgrims). He bombarded Calicut, extracted tribute, and secured trading concessions. The Strait of Hormuz was later controlled by the Portuguese under Albuquerque in 1515. The first permanent Portuguese factory in India was indeed established at Cannanore (Kannur) after the second voyage.
